subject: HealthGrid request: third‑party roster & evidence for procurement review
messages:
From: Maya Patel <security@healthgrid.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Third‑party roster & evidence request for upcoming SOW review

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the time on the call this morning. As part of our procurement security review for the upcoming SOW, we need a concise third‑party roster and a small evidence bundle for our security & procurement teams to review. Specifically we need:  

- Complete list of subprocessors (names, primary function, country of operation, whether they have access to customer data)  
- Copy of your latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted if necessary)  
- SIG or CAIQ responses covering encryption, key management, and access controls  
- Any KMS/residency statements for customer keys (even if customer‑managed)  

Can you provide a single bundle or point us to a secure location by end of week? If there are any items you cannot share, please flag them and provide a short justification for our compliance team.

Maya Patel
Security Program Manager
HealthGrid
security@healthgrid.com

[This request is tied to purchase request HG-2027-91]
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <security@healthgrid.com>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Third‑party roster & evidence request for upcoming SOW review

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We can put together a compact package and upload it to a secure share. Quick clarifications so we scope correctly:  

1) Roster format: is CSV preferred (machine readable) or would you like a PDF matrix? We can provide both but will prioritize CSV.  
2) SOC 2: we can share the latest Type II report with a standard NDA/redaction (control descriptions redacted). Will that work for procurement?
3) SIG vs CAIQ: do you need both? Our standard delivery is a completed SIG Lite + CAIQ artifacts for cryptography controls — happy to supply the SIG spreadsheet and an appended CAIQ extract for the specific questions you called out.
4) KMS proof: we have a short one‑page pdf summarizing KMS responsibilities and residency for customer‑managed keys; if you need HSM attestation we can flag that with Eng.

I’m looping in Karthik (security/compliance) and Grace (sales ops renewal) to assemble the items. We’ll aim to share a secure bundle link by Thu EOD (2027‑03‑25) unless you need it sooner.

Attachments planned: redwood_subprocessor_roster_v1.csv, SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (redacted), SIG_responses_HealthGrid.xlsx, kms_proof_summary.pdf

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior AE, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com

I’ve started a folder and uploaded a working draft (internal) — link below. Once we have the draft I’ll request a secure share for HealthGrid.

Maya — attaching the secure bundle link below and included a short manifest in the body for quick reference. If procurement/security want a DocuSign NDA we can accelerate the SOC 2 transfer; otherwise the redacted PDF in the share should be sufficient for initial review.

Secure share (expires 2027‑04‑07): https://share.redwoodinference.com/s/healthgrid/HG-2027-91-evidence

Manifest (included in the share):
- redwood_subprocessor_roster_v1.csv — 12 rows, fields: subprocessor,function,data_access,location,contract_reference,pii_touch
- SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf — redacted; auditor: Meridian Audit Co.
- SIG_responses_HealthGrid.xlsx — SIG Lite export with highlighted controls for cryptography and key mgmt
- kms_proof_summary.pdf — 1 page, describes KMS ownership, HSM usage, and residency options for hosted vs private deployments

Notes / exceptions:
- A small subset of vendor contracts include more restrictive disclosure restrictions; those vendors are marked in the CSV with "contract_sensitive" and we included a one‑line justification column.
- HSM attestation: we do not publish third‑party HSM attestation reports publicly; if HealthGrid requires deeper evidence we can arrange an on‑site or targeted call with our Infra team (contact: infra@redwoodinference.com).

Next steps: please confirm receipt and whether procurement needs an NDA signed to unlock SOC 2. If everything looks good we can map these artifacts to the SOW acceptance checklist and move to signature.

Best,
